title: Harvest dimension 1 — by energy type — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "Harvest dimension 1 — by energy type". The energy-type classifications and public figures belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: the energy-type harvest is really an energy-accounting method — follow the joules through every conversion and the books must balance. The Signature completion turns the dimension into a worked method: for any collision, write the energy ledger (in: kinetic + rest-mass + gravitational; out: heat + radiation + kinetic of debris + new rest mass), and any imbalance is either a measurement (missing energy = discovery, as with neutrinos) or an error. The record works the method on three public cases: annihilation (perfect balance), the Chicxulub scenario (partitioned), and LHC missing-energy searches (imbalance as signal).

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature "ledger-first" norm for presenting any collision result — show the energy books before the interpretation — offered as a communication proposal, not an established standard.
capabilities: Turn the energy dimension into an energy-ledger method
Work annihilation, Chicxulub, and missing-energy cases
Treat imbalance as signal-or-error, never hidden
Propose the ledger-first norm (labeled)
Keep classifications public, method here
demo:
# Ledger-first method: energy books must balance (Signature method, labeled)
def ledger(name, Ein, Eout):
    bal = sum(Ein.values()) - sum(Eout.values())
    print("%s: in=%.2e J out=%.2e J imbalance=%.2e J" % (name, sum(Ein.values()), sum(Eout.values()), bal))
    print("  imbalance = measurement (neutrinos?) or error -- investigate, don't hide")
ledger("annihilation", {"rest": 1.64e-13}, {"photons": 1.64e-13})
ledger("LHC SUSY search", {"beams": 2.2e-6}, {"visible": 1.9e-6, "missing": 0.3e-6})
print("Signature norm (proposed): show the books before the interpretation")
demo_output:
annihilation: in=1.64e-13 J out=1.64e-13 J imbalance=0.00e+00 J
  imbalance = measurement (neutrinos?) or error -- investigate, don't hide
LHC SUSY search: in=2.20e-06 J out=2.20e-06 J imbalance=0.00e+00 J
  imbalance = measurement (neutrinos?) or error -- investigate, don't hide
Signature norm (proposed): show the books before the interpretation

title: Harvest dimension 2 — by mass type — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "Harvest dimension 2 — by mass type". The mass classifications and PDG values belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: the mass-type harvest exposes the deepest public fact in the lane — that mass is not stuff but frozen energy dynamics (the proton's 99 percent). The Signature completion builds this into a teaching progression: start with weighing (rest mass), break it (invariant mass of systems), lose it (missing energy), and end with the punchline (most of your mass is gluon motion). Each step uses only public measurements, arranged as a ladder the generator can extend with new worked examples.

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature "mass-is-verb" framing — mass as something fields do, not something things have — offered as pedagogy, not physics.
capabilities: Build the mass teaching ladder from public measurements
Work the proton-mass punchline quantitatively
Offer the mass-is-verb framing as pedagogy (labeled)
Generate new worked examples on the ladder
Keep mass values public, arrangement here
demo:
# Teaching ladder: mass as something fields do (Signature pedagogy, labeled)
steps = [("weigh it", "electron 0.511 MeV on the scale"),
         ("break it", "proton 938 MeV != sum of quark masses"),
         ("lose it", "beta decay's missing energy -> neutrino"),
         ("punchline", "~99% of your mass is gluon-field energy (public QCD)")]
for i, (s, e) in enumerate(steps, 1):
    print("%d. %-10s %s" % (i, s, e))
print("Signature framing (pedagogy): mass is a verb, not a noun")
demo_output:
1. weigh it   electron 0.511 MeV on the scale
2. break it   proton 938 MeV != sum of quark masses
3. lose it    beta decay's missing energy -> neutrino
4. punchline  ~99% of your mass is gluon-field energy (public QCD)
Signature framing (pedagogy): mass is a verb, not a noun

title: Harvest dimension 3 — moving vs stationary: frames of reference — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "Harvest dimension 3 — moving vs stationary". The frame formulas belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: frame choice is the most under-taught idea in popular physics — every "paradox" dissolves when the frame is stated. The Signature completion collects the lane's frame-dependent statements (collision energy, simultaneity of detector hits, beaming directions) and shows each resolved by naming the frame. The record proposes a reading discipline: whenever a collision claim confuses you, ask "in which frame?" first.

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature "frame-first" checklist for reading any collision result, offered as a literacy tool.
capabilities: Collect the lane's frame-dependent statements
Dissolve paradoxes by naming frames
Offer the frame-first checklist (labeled)
Show what the CM frame reveals vs the lab
Keep formulas public, literacy tool here
demo:
# Frame-first checklist (Signature literacy tool, labeled)
checks = ["Which frame is the energy quoted in?",
          "Which frame is 'simultaneous' in?",
          "Which way does beaming point, and in whose frame?",
          "What does the CM frame make available that the lab hides?"]
for c in checks:
    print("?", c)
print("Discipline: name the frame before debating the claim")

? Which frame is the energy quoted in?
? Which frame is 'simultaneous' in?

Discipline: name the frame before debating the claim

title: Harvest dimension 4 — by environment factor — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "Harvest dimension 4 — by environment factor". The operating points belong to the public record; the full ranges live in item 117. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: environments are the hidden variable of experimental physics — the same collision in a different environment is a different experiment. The Signature completion works this as a transfer method: take a result, list its environmental dependencies, and ask what changes if each is varied. Worked on the LHC (what if the magnets were 16 T? — the FCC-hh question, public) and on ALICE (what if the collision were colder? — it can't be; the temperature is the point).

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature "environment-transfer" template for porting results across conditions, offered as a method proposal.
capabilities: Treat environment as the hidden variable of experiments
Work the LHC and ALICE transfer examples
Offer the environment-transfer template (labeled)
Define each result's real domain via variation
Keep operating points public, method here

# Environment-transfer template (Signature method, labeled)
template = ["1. list the result's environmental dependencies",
            "2. vary each within its public range (item 117 tables)",
            "3. mark which variations preserve the result",
            "4. the preserved set = the result's real domain"]
for t in template:
    print(t)
print("Example: LHC at 16 T magnets -> FCC-hh regime (public proposal)")

title: Harvest dimension 5 — by particle species and interaction — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "Harvest dimension 5 — by particle species and interaction". The species matrix belongs to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: the species matrix is a menu of probes, and choosing probes is the experimentalist's art. The Signature completion turns the matrix into a probe-selection method: state the physics target, list candidate probes with their trade-offs (clean vs energetic vs dense), and pick by figure of merit — the same decision the field made historically (HERA's electrons for structure, LHC's protons for discovery). The record works three historical selections as case studies.

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature probe-selection worksheet for future experiments, offered as a planning tool.
capabilities: Turn the species matrix into a probe-selection method
Work three historical probe choices as case studies
Offer the probe-selection worksheet (labeled)

title: Harvest dimension 6 — by era, detector, and outcome — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "Harvest dimension 6 — by era, detector, and outcome". The eras, detectors, and outcomes belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: the outcome classification — discoveries, confirmations, productive nulls, open questions — is really a theory of scientific progress in miniature. The Signature completion reads it as a cycle: precision confirmations corner the theory, nulls redirect effort, discoveries reset the agenda, and open questions recruit the next instruments. The record maps the lane's history onto this cycle twice (the electroweak cycle 1973-2012, the QCD cycle 1968-2005) to show the pattern repeating.

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature "progress-cycle" map for orienting new results — which phase is this result in? — offered as an interpretive tool, not as philosophy of science fact.
capabilities: Read the outcome classes as a progress cycle
Map the electroweak and QCD cycles onto it
Offer the progress-cycle orienting map (labeled)
Treat nulls as redirections in the cycle
Keep outcomes public, cycle reading here
demo:
# The progress cycle, twice around (Signature reading, labeled)
cycle = ["precision corners theory", "nulls redirect effort",
         "discovery resets agenda", "open questions recruit instruments"]
print("Electroweak cycle: neutral currents -> LEP fits -> Higgs -> hierarchy problem")
print("QCD cycle: quarks -> HERA maps -> QGP liquid -> phases at high density")
for i, ph in enumerate(cycle, 1):
    print("  %d. %s" % (i, ph))
print("Orient any new result: which phase is it in? (interpretive tool)")

Electroweak cycle: neutral currents -> LEP fits -> Higgs -> hierarchy problem
QCD cycle: quarks -> HERA maps -> QGP liquid -> phases at high density
